title: 🛡️ Extraordinas Raises $1.5 Million for a Platform That Responds to Cyberattacks Within an Hour!
body: 🛡️ Extraordinas Raises $1.5 Million for a Platform That Responds to Cyberattacks Within an Hour!
Cybersecurity startup Extraordinas has raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round from individual investors, to expand its full incident-response platform and speed up product development.

The platform helps incident response teams, managed service providers and corporate security teams manage an incident from start to finish: from the first data collection, through investigation, to reporting and recovery.

The platform covers common incident types, such as ransomware, email fraud, insider threats, cloud and identity breaches, with capabilities including one-click data collection, automatic log ingestion and linking identity to threats.

The company says its average incident resolution time is 59 minutes, and that the average cost of a data breach reached $4.4 million in 2025 — making response speed a decisive factor in reducing losses.

One of its customers is Synch IT, a technology services management company, which says the platform gives it a fast view of what happened and clear answers for its customers within minutes, so operations resume quickly.

The company was founded in August 2025 by Jay Mosotori, formerly an incident response manager at CrowdStrike, and Clark Harshbarger, a former FBI agent, with the aim of embedding years of field experience into the platform itself.
The new funding will go to product development and market expansion, while the company's success remains tied to proving consistent speed and clarity to customers.
Simply put: when a cyberattack hits, every minute of delay costs money... Will fast response become the new standard in cybersecurity?
If a single breach costs millions of dollars, is it worth it for companies to pay for a platform that resolves it in under an hour?
